options: A. O. Hume, about Indian National Congress

items.question: Which Indian Nationalist Leader is known as 'Grand Old Man of India'?
items.previous_note: "Grand Old Man of India": the title is not in NCERT/WBBSE. The exam_note states the usual answer (Naoroji) and says the books do not carry the title. Source gap.

items.question: Name the first newspaper in India.
options: Bengal Gazette / Hicky's Gazette / Hicky's Bengal Gazette
items.keyed_answer: Bengal Gazette / Hicky's Gazette / Hicky's Bengal Gazette
items.previous_note: First newspaper (Hicky's Bengal Gazette): not in the sources used; press history belongs with HIS-20. Source gap.

items.question: The British Committee of the Indian National Congress was started in 1889 under the chairmanship of:
items.previous_note: British Committee of the INC (1889) under Wedderburn: not in the sources (WBBSE mentions Wedderburn only as Hume's 1913 biographer). Source gap.

items.question: The historical importance of the second session of the INC held in Calcutta in 1886 was that—
options: There was merger between the INC and the National Conference.
It was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.
The great scholar Rajendralal Mitra was the President of its local Reception Committee.
items.keyed_answer: There was merger between the INC and the National Conference.
items.previous_note: 1886 Calcutta session / merger with the National Conference: not in the sources (WBBSE gives only the 1883 National Conference). Source gap.

items.question: Dadabhai Naoroji was elected to the British House of Commons as a member of the _______ party.
items.previous_note: Naoroji's party (Liberal): the sources only say he was the first Indian elected to the House of Commons and an MP in 1892. Source gap.

items.question: Who observed: "The Congress is in reality a civil war without arms"?
items.previous_note: "Civil war without arms" is not in the sources; WBBSE p. 557 only says Syed Ahmad Khan was directly opposed to the Congress. Source gap.

items.question: The word Congress was borrowed from
options: North American History, to connote an assembly of people.
The Congress of World Religions at Chicago.
items.keyed_answer: North American History, to connote an assembly of people.
items.previous_note: Origin of the word "Congress": not in the sources. Source gap.

items.question: Which of the following are known as the Bombay Triumvirate?
options: B. G. Tilak, G. K. Gokhale and M. B. Namjoshi
Ferozshah Mehta, K. T. Telang and Badruddin Tyabji
B. G. Tilak, G. G. Agarkar and G. H. Deshmukh
Dadabhai Naoroji, K. T. Telang and R. G. Bhandarker
items.keyed_answer: Ferozshah Mehta, K. T. Telang and Badruddin Tyabji
items.previous_note: Bombay Triumvirate (Mehta, Telang, Tyabji): term not in the sources (hess208 names Mehta and Tyabji, and Telang in Wacha's letter). Source gap.
